retellable.title: Secret dinners that built a dyad
retellable.summary: To keep smaller Fremont from losing out on funding, Wheeler secretly met Hayward PIC Annabel Anderson-Imbert in a faraway restaurant to plan merging the two into one service area. After months with a consultant they announced the dyad, merged chief roles, and opened the long-idle Fremont hospital.
retellable.quote: So I approached her confidentially to present the idea, and we met in the evening restaurant far away so that we wouldn't be discovered, etc. etc.
retellable.why: Shows how a major structural change was quietly planned before going public.

retellable.title: Eight former patients became physicians
retellable.summary: As the only African American pediatrician in the Hayward-Oakland area, Wheeler's general pediatrics practice filled quickly. Eight of the children he cared for in those three years became physicians, including three brothers.
retellable.quote: I have eight patients from my three years of doing general peds that are now physicians, three from one family, three brothers. So it was quite, quite a time to be a role model
retellable.why: A concrete picture of representation and role modeling in care.

retellable.title: Too nice to lead?
retellable.summary: During his PIC selection, Dr. Caulfield relayed that physicians feared Wheeler was too nice to do the hard parts of leadership. Wheeler answered that leaders need not be mean-spirited and kept that question in mind when choosing other leaders.
retellable.quote: physicians, they said you were such a nice guy that they didn't know that you would be able to do the hard part or the hard stuff, uh, to provide leadership.
retellable.why: A memorable leadership lesson on kindness and accountability.

retellable.title: Learning not to shake hands
retellable.summary: At Fremont, community representatives were invited to teach staff how their communities preferred to receive care. Wheeler learned that as a male physician he should not touch Muslim mothers, changing his usual exam-room greeting.
retellable.quote: my normal thing was to walk into an exam room and shake hands with the parents, say hello and then, you know, touch or interact with the child. But for Muslim women, I couldn't touch her
retellable.why: A simple, teachable example of culturally responsive care.
